name: Obsolescence

subjectOf.text: Formal rulemaking in the existing regulatory infrastructure is almost always too time consuming, because product innovation moves fast enough that regulations covering an innovative product are obsolete before they are finalized.
subjectOf.abstract: Formal rulemaking in the existing regulatory infrastructure is almost always too time-consuming (Sunstein 1999, McGarity 1992) because the speed of product innovation often makes regulations pertaining to an innovative product obsolete before such regulations are finalized
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation for Innovation (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2831040
scope_conditions: formal rulemaking directed at fast moving innovative products

subjectOf.text: The benefits of coding existing law into smart contracts are only temporary, because as smart contracting evolves over time fewer smart contracting solutions will have a real world equivalent.
subjectOf.abstract: The benefits of this hybrid approach are only temporary. As smart contracting evolves over time, fewer smart contracting solutions will have a real-world equivalent.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Craig Calcaterra, Crypto Transaction Dispute Resolution (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2992962
scope_conditions: over the course of smart contracting's evolution

subjectOf.text: Because blockchain is transparent, verifiable, self-authenticating and self-enforcing, transactions can settle instantaneously at near zero cost, and it is this combination plus technology-driven democratized trust that drove the financial industry's large blockchain investments out of fear of obsolescence.
subjectOf.abstract: Blockchain technology is transparent, verifiable, self- authenticating, and self-enforcing, financial transactions can be executed instantaneously at near zero transaction costs, increasing the efficiency for business and individuals exponentially.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Financial Technology and Hedge Funds (2019). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3409548

subjectOf.text: The speed of smart contracting and associated DAO revisions will render regulations aimed at morphing decentralized systems obsolete before static centralized regulations are even finalized.
subjectOf.abstract: The speed of smart contracting and the associated DAO revisions will make regulations pertaining to morphing and evolving decentralized systems obsolete before static centralized regulations are finalized.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain-Based Corporate Governance (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3441904

subjectOf.text: Expectations of enhanced regulatory oversight fail because the accelerating evolution of AI agents, which will soon dominate financial transactions, renders static legal frameworks obsolete.
subjectOf.abstract: The expectation of enhanced regulatory oversight fails to account for the accelerating evolution of AI agents, which will soon dominate financial transactions, rendering static legal frameworks obsolete.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How can we Best Monitor AI Agents (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5245185
scope_conditions: AI agents dominating financial transaction volume

subjectOf.text: Static codification is fundamentally incompatible with the governance needs of exponentially evolving digital technologies.
subjectOf.abstract: Static codification is fundamentally incompatible with the governance needs of exponentially evolving digital technologies.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The UDLC DAO Operationalizing a Continuously Evolving Universal Digital Law Codex Through Weighted (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5887242
scope_conditions: digital technology domains that advance on monthly cycles
